Understanding the OBJ File Format – A Simple Explanation
Posted by
sychev23021983
On August 26, 2022

OBJ is a text-based 3D file format used to exchange surface geometry between applications. An .obj file can describe vertices, polygon faces, texture coordinates and normals.

The format is commonly used for static models in visualization, scanning and 3D-printing workflows. Appearance data may depend on accompanying material and texture files. OBJ does not preserve skeletal animation, cameras or lights as a complete scene.

OBJ FILE FORMAT: UTILIZATION IN 3D PRINTING

OBJ can supply geometry for 3D printing, but importing an OBJ file does not guarantee that the slicer will retain its materials or textures. For example, PrusaSlicer imports OBJ geometry while ignoring material and texture information.

The format’s support for free-form curves and surfaces does not guarantee smaller files or greater printing precision. Check which geometry representations your software accepts, and ensure the printable mesh defines a solid with adequate wall thickness.

STL, OBJ and 3MF serve different exchange and project needs. PrusaSlicer supports all three and recommends 3MF for saving projects; the choice should follow the target workflow.

OBJ FILE FORMAT: USAGE IN 3D GRAPHICS APPLICATIONS

OBJ is suitable for transferring static assets into a rendering or modeling scene. The receiving application provides the scene’s cameras, lights and animation setup.

When a transfer must retain animation or broader scene data, consider an exchange format such as FBX. Native project formats may be more appropriate when preserving application-specific features is essential.

For a geographic example, the USA terrain model is supplied with C4D geometry, OBJ versions at three levels of detail and TIF textures. The illustrated C4D-to-OBJ terrain workflow covers mesh export and texture handling.

ADVANTAGES OF THE OBJ FILE FORMAT

OBJ is widely supported for static mesh exchange, but import behavior varies between applications. Materials may need adjustment, and support for free-form geometry or extended material properties should be checked in the target software.

Wavefront OBJ is a text-based geometry format. Material definitions are commonly stored in an associated MTL file, with texture images supplied separately.
